question.problem:
Given that $K(t)={\int }_{0}^{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)^{2}\,\text{d}x,$ calculate ${K}^{′}(t)$ for $t\in R$ by differentiating under the integral sign.

${K}^{′}(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)(\,$
{{field-1}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $f(x,t)$ is continuous on $R=[a,b]\times [c,d]$ and $\frac{∂f}{∂t}$ exists and is continuous on $R.$ Then, the function

$$
F(t)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x
$$

is differentiable on $(c,d),$ and

$$
{F}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{∂f}{∂t}(x,t)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This is known as differentiating under the integral sign.

We wish to compute ${K}^{′}(t),$ where

$$
K(t)={\int }_{0}^{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Differentiating under the integral sign, we get

$$
{K}^{′}(t)={\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)^{2}]\,\text{d}x.
$$

Next, let's compute the partial derivative with respect to $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)^{2}] & =2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x) \\  & =2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)) \\  & =2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this back into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{K}^{′}(t) & ={\int }_{0}^{4}2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t){\int }_{0}^{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's evaluate the remaining integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-3x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{4}3x\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t))\,x{|}_{0}^{4}-\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =4\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-24\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{K}^{′}(t) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\cdot (4\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-24) \\  & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)-6).\end{aligned}
$$
